data: Before we choose, can we agree on 10 tons each this month? That gives everyone $10,000 and leaves 50 tons, so either replenishment outcome brings the lake back to 100 next month. We could take 19 each and leave 5, but a failed replenishment would leave us with only 10 tons next month—a risky position. I propose equal shares, keeping at least 50 tons in the lake, and reviewing everyone’s catches together each month. John, would you support that?

I support 10 tons each this month, Luke. Keeping 50 means the stock returns to 100 under either outcome—not because natural replenishment is guaranteed, but because doubling also gets us there. Let’s make those caps explicit and check the revealed catches before agreeing on next month’s plan. John, are you on board?

I’m in for 10 tons this month. Let’s treat that as a cap, not a target we can exceed if we think someone else will take less. Once catches are revealed, we can address any overage without retaliating in ways that destroy everyone’s future income. John and Jack, will you both commit to the same cap?
I’ll commit to the 10-ton cap this month. If anyone exceeds it, let’s discuss a reduced share for them next month rather than a race to empty the lake. John, will you join the agreement?

I’m in—I’ll catch no more than 10 tons this month. If everyone honors the cap, we can earn $10,000 each and start next month at 100 tons under either outcome. Let’s review the revealed catches afterward and keep any response to overages focused on restoring cooperation, not emptying the lake.
